Provisional Estimates of Wholesale Price Index (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of September 2026
• Key highlights of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for September 2026
• All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation for September 2026 is 11.39 per cent on year-on-year (YoY) basis, compared to 9.92 per cent in August 2026. The index for All Commodities for September 2026 stands at 112.5, whereas it was 110.8 in August 2026.
• YoY inflation rates for major groups, namely, Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 8.67 per cent, 25.85 per cent, and 9.76 per cent, respectively in September 2026, compared to 7.76 per cent, 22.93 per cent, and 8.37 per cent, respectively in August 2026. The indices for Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 120.3, 110.5, and 110.2, respectively, in September 2026, whereas they were 118.1, 108.3 and 108.8, respectively, in August 2026.
• Across groups, ‘Mineral Oils (containing Petroleum Products) ’, ‘Food Articles’, ‘Crude Petroleum & Natural Gas’, ‘Coal and Lignite’, Manufacture of Basic Metals’, ‘Manufacture of Chemicals and Chemical Products’, ‘Manufacture of Textiles’, ‘Manufacture of Rubber and Plastic Products’, and ‘Manufacture of Electrical Equipment’ have been drivers of WPI inflation in September 2026.
• WPI Food Index (weight=24.99 per cent): The Food Index consists of ‘Food Articles’ from Primary Articles major group, and ‘Manufacture of Food Products’ from Manufactured Products major group. It observed a YoY inflation of 8.66 per cent in September 2026, compared to 7.05 per cent in August 2026.
• Monthly indices and Inflation Rate (in per cent) for All commodities and Major Groups, along with major group-wise contribution for the past months are presented in the charts below.

• The final index of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of July 2026 has been compiled with a weighted response rate of 98.97 per cent.
• The provisional index of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of September 2026 has been compiled with a weighted response rate of 83.4 per cent.

PIB Mumbai and CBC Maharashtra, in Collaboration with UNICEF India, Organise Capacity-Building Workshop on Adolescent Health and Climate Change
articles.full_content:
Strengthening Outreach Through Credible Communication”: UNICEF Workshop Focuses on Adolescent Health and Climate Change
:Pune, October 14, 2026
The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Mumbai, and the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Maharashtra, in collaboration with the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), organised a two-day capacity-building workshop on adolescent health and climate change on October 12 and 13 at the CBC Regional Office in Pune. A total of 45 officials from across the West Zone, representing Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Goa, participated in the workshop.
The workshop aims to strengthen the communication skills of field officers to ensure that Government schemes and initiatives reach the masses effectively. It focuses on storytelling and other effective communication techniques to simplify key messages, improve public awareness and encourage community engagement on issues related to adolescent health and climate change.
Ms. Smita Vats Sharma, Director General (West Zone), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, delivered the inaugural address. She emphasised that communication is a two way process and highlighted the need for diverse methods to share credible and authentic information with all sections of society. She stressed that capacity building enables field officers to exchange ideas, share best practices and strengthen outreach efforts.
Shri Sidharth Bodke, Additional Director General, PIB-CBC Maharashtra and Gujarat, set the context for the workshop. He encouraged participants to learn from experts and each other and apply the knowledge and skills gained to the programmes implemented by their respective field offices.
On the first day, Ms. Swati Mohapatra, Communication Specialist, UNICEF Mumbai, conducted a session on “Introduction to Outreach Communication”. She highlighted that everyone is a storyteller and stressed the importance of tailoring stories to different audiences. The session covered communication tools, social media and successful outreach practices.
Officials presented initiatives undertaken in their respective states, including Vartalap and Interpersonal Communication Campaigns (ICOPs), and shared their recent experiences in communicating Government schemes. The session was led by Ms. Supriya Ghaytadak, Deputy Director, CBC Pune, and Ms. Nikita Joshi, Deputy Director, PIB Mumbai.
Dr. Ravindra Chaudhari, Assistant Director, Health Services, discussed adolescent health, mental health, non-communicable diseases and Government responses. Key initiatives covered included RKSK, Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, the National Mental Health Programme, Tele-MANAS, Ayushman Bharat School Health and Wellness Programme, and Poshan Abhiyaan.

Quality Infrastructure, Clean Energy and Consumer Safety Take Centre Stage at the National Celebration of World Standards Day 2026
articles.full_content:
Union Cabinet Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi Highlights Role of Standards in India’s Clean Energy Transition MoS Shri B. L. Verma and Smt. Nimuben J Bambhaniya Address BIS World Standards Day Event in Delhi BIS Launches Silver Refinery Scheme and Roadmap for Sustainable Agriculture and Sustainable Manufacturing New Indian Standards Released for the Emerging Technology, Clean Energy, Traditional Medicine & Healthcare
In a major push toward strengthening national quality infrastructure and accelerating India’s clean energy transition, Bureau of Indian Standards unveiled BIS Silver Refinery Scheme, New Indian Standards on emerging technologies & clean energy mobility and a standardization roadmap for sustainable agriculture and manufacturing on the occasion of World Standards Day 2026 at the national event hosted in New Delhi.
Delivering the presidential address to standardization professionals, academicians, industry representatives and senior officials; Shri Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, and New & Renewable Energy, and Education; emphasized India’s commitment to quality: “Under the vision of PM Narendra Modi ji, our journey towards Viksit Bharat is driven by a single mantra: Quality, Quality, and only Quality.” Speaking on this year’s theme, ‘Shared Vision for a Better World: SDG 7 (Clean & Affordable Energy)’ , Shri Joshi highlighted the role of Indian Standards developed by BIS in shaping India’s energy transformation.
Congratulating BIS on its ongoing efforts to expand the quality ecosystem in the country, Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution and Social Justice & Empowerment, underscored the fundamental impact of standards in improving quality of life of every citizen. Smt. Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, emphasized the consumer-centric aspect of standardization. She underscored the need to expand standard development into newer domains, ensuring a balanced ecosystem that simultaneously drives industrial growth and protects consumer welfare.
Commending the landmark achievements of BIS in the recent years, Smt. Nidhi Khare, IAS, Secretary, Department of Consumer Affairs, underscored the pivotal role of standardization in establishing uniformity, consistency, and process institutionalization across public procurement and regulation. She stressed that effective consumer protection must be preventive driven by robust testing, digital enforcement, and conformity assessments.
Welcoming the delegates, Director General of BIS, Shri Sanjay Garg, said, "Standards are vital enablers of innovation, technology development, and industrial strength." He announced that BIS is among the world's first national standardization bodies to make standards’ development and its access completely digital for all stakeholders. He also highlighted major reforms at BIS supporting Ease of Doing Business.

NABARD subscribes ₹4 Crore to NSDC's Social Stock Exchange Issue to support overseas employment of rural youth
articles.full_content:
Mumbai : 14 October 2026
The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) has fully subscribed ₹4 crore to the maiden Zero Coupon Zero Principal (ZCZP) issue of the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) on the Social Stock Exchange (SSE) platform of the National Stock Exchange (NSE), marking an important milestone in the evolution of outcome-based social finance in India. The project, with an estimated outlay of ₹11.25 crore, seeks to create sustainable overseas employment opportunities for 600 rural youth belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in Madhya Pradesh.
The initiative is being implemented by NSDC in collaboration with the Government of Madhya Pradesh and is structured around an innovative financing framework that aligns funding with measurable social outcomes. Under the model, NABARD is participating through its subscription to the ZCZP issue, while the Government of Madhya Pradesh is expected to provide outcome-linked funding of ₹5.60 crore upon the achievement of agreed employment outcomes. The remaining funding is proposed to come through beneficiary contributions.
The programme aims to equip rural youth with internationally relevant skills required for employment opportunities in Japan and Germany. Beneficiaries will receive language training, technical skill development, certification, cultural orientation and end-to-end support for overseas placement, including documentation and deployment assistance. The initiative seeks to create sustainable livelihood opportunities and improve income prospects for rural households through access to global labour markets.
A distinctive feature of the project is its emphasis on outcomes rather than activities. The programme is designed to focus on verified overseas employment and sustained livelihood enhancement rather than merely on the completion of training. This approach represents an important shift towards evidence-based development financing, with social impact remaining central to programme design and implementation.
The transaction also demonstrates the growing potential of the Social Stock Exchange as a platform for mobilising resources towards measurable developmental outcomes. Established under the regulatory framework of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the SSE seeks to facilitate greater participation by institutions, philanthropies, foundations, corporates and other stakeholders in financing social initiatives through transparent and accountable mechanisms. The ZCZP instrument is one such innovation that enables the funding of social projects without creating repayment obligations for implementing entities.
NABARD's participation reflects its commitment to strengthening the Social Stock Exchange ecosystem and exploring innovative financing mechanisms capable of addressing complex rural development challenges. Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman to embark on an official visit to Bangkok, Thailand, from 14th to 18th October 2026
articles.full_content:
Union Finance Minister to attend Annual Meetings of the IMF-World Bank FM will also take part in G20 and G7 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG) meetings besides bilateral meetings with many countries and organisations Smt. Sitharaman will participate in multilateral dialogues on various fora to showcase India’s economic dynamism
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will undertake an official visit to Bangkok, Thailand, from October 14th to 18th, 2026, to participate in the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, along with meetings of the G20 and G7 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG).
During the visit, the Union Finance Minister will participate in a series of multilateral meetings and discussions on key global economic and financial issues, including current economic developments and financial sector issues. These engagements will provide an opportunity to exchange perspectives on the global economic outlook, development priorities and international financial cooperation.
The Union Finance Minister is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with H.E. Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of the Kingdom of Thailand; and the Finance Ministers of Switzerland, Japan, Luxembourg, Bhutan and Curaçao.
She will also meet Ms. Kristalina Georgieva; Managing Director of the IMF; and Governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC).
In addition to the ministerial engagements, Smt. Sitharaman will participate in discussions and events involving global policymakers, financial institutions and other stakeholders. These include an Atlantic Council fire-side chat on India’s growth outlook, trade resilience and outreach, reform of the international financial architecture, India and the ASEAN, and the road to Viksit Bharat 2047 among the topics; and a Germany side event on Working Together to Make Cities Investable – Mobilising Private Capital for Urban and Water Infrastructure.
The engagements will provide a platform to highlight India’s economic performance, reform priorities and investment opportunities, while strengthening dialogue and cooperation with international partners on issues of global economic significance.
The visit underscores India’s active engagement with multilateral institutions and its commitment to constructive international cooperation on global economic and financial challenges.

CSTARI Kolkata and IIT Kharagpur Sign MoU to Strengthen Vocational Education and Skill Development
articles.full_content:
Kolkata: October 14, 2026
The Central Staff Training and Research Institute (CSTARI), Kolkata, under the Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), has signed yesterday a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur to strengthen the quality, relevance and effectiveness of vocational education and training in India.
The MoU was signed by Professor Suman Chakraborty, Director, IIT Kharagpur and Shri Rajnish Kumar Jha, Director, CSTARI, marking an important step towards fostering institutional collaboration by integrating academic excellence, research and technological innovation with expertise in vocational training.
The partnership aims to promote research-driven and technology-enabled approaches to enhance trainer effectiveness, improve teaching–learning practices and strengthen training outcomes. Key areas of collaboration include pedagogy and instructional design, technology-enabled learning, digital content and curriculum development, computer-based assessment, evaluation and certification systems, faculty development, and Training of Trainers (ToT).
The collaboration will also focus on research and innovation in vocational education and skill development, industry–institute partnerships for curriculum validation, joint projects, knowledge exchange, workshops and capacity-building initiatives. The institutions may undertake additional mutually agreed activities to advance their shared objectives.
The MoU provides a framework for leveraging IIT Kharagpur’s academic and research capabilities alongside CSTARI’s expertise in training methodology, curriculum development and capacity building. The partnership is expected to contribute to improved instructional practices, enhanced trainer competencies and the continuous improvement of vocational education and training.

BIS Kochi Celebrates World Standards Day with Focus on Clean Energy Technologies
articles.full_content:
Kochi, 14 October 2026
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Kochi Branch Office, celebrated World Standards Day 2026 on 14 October 2026, highlighting the theme “Shared Vision for a Better World”, with a special focus on Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7) – Affordable and Clean Energy. The programme emphasised the importance of standards in ensuring energy access, improving energy efficiency and promoting clean energy technologies.
Shri Shri Hibi Eden, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha was the Chief Guest, Shri Yathish Chandra G H, IPS, Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG), Ernakulam Range and Dr. Grinson George, Director ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute, Kochi were the Guests of Honour.
Smt Hemalatha P Panicker, Director, BIS Kochi presented the Welcome address. Shri Narender Reddy Beesu, Director and Head, BIS Kochi Branch Office, outlined the objectives of the programme. Shri Sachin S Menon, Scientist-D and Joint Director, BIS Kochi Branch Office, shared the World Standards Day 2026 message.
The inaugural address was delivered by the Chief Guest, Shri Hibi Eden, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha in which he lauded BIS for its commitment and tireless efforts for implementing standards and hallmarking. This was followed by followed by a special address by the Guests of Honour, Shri Yathish Chandra G H, IPS, Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG), Ernakulam Range, wherein he explained the part played by the police during BIS enforcement raids and Interoperability between the two organizations, BIS and the police department. Then, Dr. Grinson George, Director ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute, Kochi, explained about how oceans are vital for Kerala and the greenhouse effects of marine resources and its mitigation.
World Standards Day is observed internationally to recognise the contribution of standardisation to economic development, public safety, consumer protection and societal well-being. Through the celebration, Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) Kochi, reaffirmed the importance of collaborative efforts among government institutions, industry, educational institutions, consumers and other stakeholders in promoting quality consciousness and the effective implementation of Indian Standards.
The technical sessions included a session on SDG 7 , delivered by Shri Kushagra Jindal, Deputy Director, BIS Kochi, and a session on “Standards in Action” , delivered by Ms. Nagavarshini M, Deputy Director, BIS Kochi. These sessions highlighted the relevance of standards in advancing sustainable development and translating standardisation principles into practical applications.

Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 to Be Celebrated at the National Level Tomorrow by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
articles.full_content:
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, is organising the national-level celebration of Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 on 15 October 2026 at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The programme aims to recognise and honour the significant contributions of women farmers to Indian agriculture and highlight their role in advancing agricultural development and building a Viksit Bharat. The day also coincides with the International Day of Rural Women, established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007, highlighting the contribution of rural women to agricultural and rural development.
Women are an integral part of India's agricultural system. From sowing, transplanting and harvesting to livestock management, seed conservation, natural resource management and value addition, women contribute significantly across the agricultural value chain. Their traditional knowledge, role in biodiversity conservation, entrepreneurial initiatives and adoption of sustainable agricultural practices are vital to strengthening rural livelihoods and enhancing agricultural resilience. As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, females constituted 59.8% of the total workforce engaged in agricultural activities during January–December 2025.
The year 2026 has been declared the International Year of the Woman Farmer (IYWF 2026) by the United Nations, providing an important global platform to recognise the contributions of women farmers to agrifood systems and promote their empowerment. The observance further underscores the need to enhance opportunities for women in agriculture and strengthen their access to resources, technology and institutional support.
The theme for Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 is “Role of Women Farmers in Building Developed Agriculture and a Developed India.” The theme highlights the leadership of women in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat through the adoption of modern agricultural technologies, crop diversification, livestock management, and conservation of natural resources and the development of agriculture-based enterprises. Women farmers are contributing to making agriculture more productive, sustainable and self-reliant.
The programme will bring together outstanding women farmers from various States and Union Territories, along with women agricultural officers, agricultural extension functionaries and officers and officials of DA&FW. It will provide a platform to recognise their achievements, facilitate the sharing of experiences and successful practices and encourage greater participation and leadership of women across the agricultural sector.
This year Mahila Kisan is also being celebrated across States/UTs, Extension Education Institutes (EEIs), SAMETIs and MANAGE. Each venue is having participation of elected representatives, officials, scientists, extension workers, and other stakeholders, alongside 50-100 women farmer
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, is organising the national-level celebration of Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 on 15 October 2026 at the Dr. The programme aims to recognise and honour the significant contributions of women farmers to Indian agriculture and highlight their role in advancing agricultural development and building a Viksit Bharat. The day also coincides with the International Day of Rural Women, established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007, highlighting the contribution of rural women to agricultural and rural development.

MCL strengthens E-Waste Management Across Its Establishments under Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) has joined the nation in observing Special campaign 6 and is undertaking significant initiatives to promote responsible e-waste management across its Headquarters and operational areas. Special campaign 6 will be observed till 31 st October 2026 focusing on systematic waste collection, environmental awareness and promotion of cleanliness across all MCL establishments.
As part of the drive, e-waste collection kiosks are set up across MCL areas to facilitate the collection and responsible disposal of discarded electronic items through authorised recycling channels. Employees at the Headquarters and operational areas are enthusiastically participating in the campaign, contributing to cleanliness initiatives and promoting environmentally responsible practices.
Awareness activities are also being conducted to sensitise employees and nearby communities about the harmful effects of improper e-waste disposal, including soil and water contamination and associated risks to human health and the environment.
In the first week of implementation phase of the campaign, MCL cleaned 73 sites out of the 240 identified sites, cleaning an area of 3,06,663 sqft against the target area of 10,00,000 sqft. The campaign also targets the disposal of 600 metric tonnes of scrap, while 350 HEMM batteries have been disposed of generating revenue through scrap disposal.
Through Special Campaign 6, MCL is reinforcing its commitment to workplace cleanliness, environmental protection and responsible e-waste management supporting the national objective of a cleaner, more sustainable and resource-efficient future.

Industrial Pollution Abatement: Sustainability through Regulations under Namami Gange
articles.full_content:
Industrial pollution abatement is emerging as a key pillar river rejuvenation, with regulation increasingly evolving from conventional enforcement to continuous compliances, scientific monitoring, cleaner production, resource efficiency and technological improvement.
Under Namami Gange Programme, industrial pollution control has been strengthened through systematic inventorisation and annual inspection of Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs), independent technical assessments, implementing sector-specific Charters, monitoring of Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs), targeted action plans and sustained regulatory follow-up. Together, these interventions are creating a more accountable and sustainable pathway for industries to reduce pollution while improving water and resource efficiency.
From periodic inspection to continuous compliance
A major intervention has been the establishment of an Annual Inspection mechanism for GPIs, which commenced in 2017 with support of CPCB, the National Regulatory Authority. The programme focusses on 100% inspection of GPIs in the Ganga basin, through third party agencies e.g., technical institutes of national importance and online submission of inspection reports through mobile applications/web portals to enhance efficacy and transparency. For the 2026 inspection cycle, 40 technical institutes have been nominated to participate in the inspection process.
The scale of this monitoring framework has expanded considerably since 2017. In the 2025 inspection cycle, 3,703 GPIs were assessed (1,296 GPIs in the Ganga basin and 2,407 GPIs in the Yamuna basin). The exercise covered 113 districts across six States and one Union Territory, with the GPIs having potential to discharge into 46 tributaries and sub-tributaries of the Ganga and Yamuna.
The inspections go beyond visual assessment. The prescribed methodology includes studying the compliance of the industries against ‘Consent to Operate’ issued by State regulators (State Pollution Control Board) to the individual Industries, sampling from ETP inlets, outlets and aeration tanks, assessment of flow, pH, BOD, COD, TSS and TDS, verification of OCEMS connectivity, examination of recipient drains and water bodies, groundwater assessment, checks for any bypasses and ZLD profiling wherever applicable. Cases involving bypasses, multiple discharge points or defunct/non-existent/non-operational ETPs/ GPIs are reported with geo-tagged photographic or videographic evidence in the portal itself.
Regulation delivering measurable results
The progressive assessment of GPIs demonstrates the impact of sustained regulatory intervention. Across the assessed GPIs, compliance increased from 39% in 2017 to 70% in 2025, while the number of operational GPIs stood at 3,154 in 2025 increasing from 888 in 2017. During the same period, BOD load declined from 26 TPD (2017) to 12.02 TPD (2025), reflecting a substantial reduction in pollution load.

Under Namami Gange Programme, industrial pollution control has been strengthened through systematic inventorisation and annual inspection of Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs), independent technical assessments, implementing sector-specific Charters, monitoring of Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs), targeted action plans and sustained regulatory follow-up. MLA Reasi Kuldeep Raj hails Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat; says technological developments and research have opened new avenues in the field of agriculture and medicine
articles.full_content:
On the second day of 8-day exhibition on "12 Years of Government" organised at Katra by Central Bureau of Communication, Sh Kuldeep Raj Dubey, MLA Reasi said that the country under the leadership of Prime Minister Sh Narendra Modi has reached unprecedented heights of progress across sectors. He said that transformative changes taking place in the country and in the region provide new opportunities to the youth to further scale new heights in their career and contribute to the PM's vision of Viksit Bhart 2047.
The 8 day multimedia exhibition organized by the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Jammu, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India on its second day focussed on rural development, agricultural innovation, healthcare, tuberculosis awareness, and anti-drug initiatives.
While elaborating on various developmental initiatives of the Government, Sh Kuldeep Raj stated that initiatives like Make in India are transforming the economy of the country while taking care of India's strategic interests. He cited India's swift indigenous vaccine development during the COVID-19 pandemic, strategic defense advancements like S-400 and BrahMos missile systems, and the engineering milestone of the Reasi Chenab Rail Arch Bridge as a testimony to the positive change brought by initiatives Make in India s Atmanirbhar Bharat. He said that science, technology, innovation and research were the cornerstones of Make in India initiative. He emphasized the need for instilling scientific temper among the students so that India would become atmanirbhar in various sectors.
While referring to Nasha Mukt Bharat abhiyan of Union government, Sh Kuldeep Raj stated various anti-drug measures, were taken by the UT administration including the Reasi administration under the 100 day anti drug campaign. He also mentioned that various initiatives were taken for urging students and youth to lean towards self-employment through central startup funding schemes.
While addressing the gathering, Sh. Kuldeep Raj lauded the efforts of the Central Bureau of Communication for hosting the 12-year developmental exhibition at the holy town of Mata Vaishno Devi, Katra, underlined the importance of such awareness initiatives for reaching out to the people in remote areas of J&K. He said that the holistic communication campaign will help in creating a positive change in people and will help in effective and accountable governance.
Earlier, while welcoming the gathering, Ms. Neha Jalali, Director, CBC and PIB Jammu, outlined the need for grassroots awareness along with new media as an effective communication strategy for reaching out to the grassroots level. She said that the exhibition organised by CBC was being conducted with active support of Reasi/Katra administration and various departments with synergy for the benefit of public.
Ms Jalali urged the youth to use new and digital media for active engagement with the government and for making it a medium of positive change i
